lessons.title: Les êtres vivants autour de nous
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify and distinguish between living and non-living things in their environment

opening.activity: Living things hunt - students point to living and non-living items in the classroom
opening.visualSupports: living vs non-living chart with pictures

main.activity: hands-on sorting exploration of classroom items into living and non-living categories
main.visualSupports: large sorting chart, picture cards with living/non-living examples

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify basic living characteristics (grows, needs food/water)?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Move to comparing plant and animal needs
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use more concrete examples like pets vs toys

closing.activity: Circle sharing - each student shares one living thing they found

troubleshooting.then: Use movement and sound cues - living things can move and make sounds

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding the difference between living pets, plants, and toys or furniture at home

lessons.title: De quoi ont besoin les plantes pour vivre?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify that plants need water, sunlight, and air to stay alive and healthy

opening.activity: Plant observation - examining classroom plants and discussing what keeps them healthy
opening.visualSupports: plant needs poster with sun, water drop, and air symbols

main.activity: hands-on exploration creating plant needs diagrams and observing plant placement near windows
main.visualSupports: illustrated plant needs chart, before/after plant photos

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand why plants are placed near windows?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore what happens when plants don't get enough light
decisionPoints.ifNo: Demonstrate by moving plant away from light source

closing.activity: Plant needs song - singing about water, sun, and air while doing actions

troubleshooting.then: Use wind demonstration with ribbons to show air movement

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding why parents water house plants and put them near windows

lessons.title: Expérience: les plantes et l'eau
lessons.oneGoal: Students will conduct a simple experiment to observe how plants react when they have or don't have water

opening.activity: Prediction making - what will happen to plants with and without water?
opening.visualSupports: experiment setup diagram showing two plants

main.activity: hands-on science experiment setting up watered and unwatered plant observations
main.visualSupports: step-by-step experiment chart, daily observation tracking sheet

decisionPoints.question: Are students making accurate predictions about plant water needs?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them predict timeline for visible changes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Guide them with leading questions about thirsty feelings

closing.activity: Initial observations recording - drawing what both plants look like today

troubleshooting.then: Compare to trying different foods to see which you like better

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning why gardens need watering and what happens when plants don't get enough water

lessons.title: Les plantes ont besoin de lumière
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that plants need light to grow and will observe what happens without sunlight

opening.activity: Light hunt - finding all the light sources that help our classroom plants
opening.visualSupports: light source identification chart

main.activity: hands-on exploration creating light and dark conditions for plant observation
main.visualSupports: light experiment setup photos, plant growth comparison charts

decisionPoints.question: Do students notice plants leaning toward light sources?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore why plants move toward light
decisionPoints.ifNo: Demonstrate with classroom plants near windows

closing.activity: Light needs discussion - sharing observations about plant placement and light

troubleshooting.then: Compare to how students feel energetic in sunshine vs tired in dark rooms

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding why plants lean toward windows and why they grow better outside

lessons.title: De quoi ont besoin les animaux pour vivre?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify that animals need food, water, air, and shelter to stay alive and healthy

opening.activity: Pet care discussion - sharing how students care for pets or stuffed animals
opening.visualSupports: animal needs poster with food, water, shelter, air symbols

main.activity: hands-on exploration matching animals with their needs using picture cards and sorting
main.visualSupports: animal habitat pictures, pet care routine chart

decisionPoints.question: Can students connect animal needs to plant needs they already learned?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Create Venn diagram comparing plant and animal needs
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on most obvious needs like food and water first

closing.activity: Animal needs role play - acting out feeding, watering, and sheltering pets

troubleshooting.then: Compare to their own bedroom providing safety and comfort

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding why pets need food bowls, water dishes, and safe places to sleep

lessons.title: Les bébés animaux grandissent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe that baby animals grow into adult animals and need special care when young

opening.activity: Baby animal picture sharing - looking at photos of baby animals and their parents
opening.visualSupports: animal growth timeline display

main.activity: hands-on exploration sequencing animal growth stages and discussing care needs
main.visualSupports: animal life cycle posters, before and after growth photos

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand that baby animals need extra protection?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore how parents care for babies differently than adults
decisionPoints.ifNo: Compare to how they needed more care when they were babies

closing.activity: Growth story telling - each student shares about an animal baby growing up

troubleshooting.then: Use their own baby photos to show how they have grown

lessons.realWorldConnection: Connecting to students' own growth and observing how pets or farm animals change

lessons.title: Comment prendre soin d'une plante?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn practical ways to care for plants by providing water, light, and proper conditions

opening.activity: Plant care routine demonstration - showing proper watering and positioning techniques
opening.visualSupports: plant care checklist with pictures

main.activity: hands-on plant care practice - students water, position, and check their assigned plants
main.visualSupports: step-by-step care instruction cards, plant health identification chart

decisionPoints.question: Are students watering appropriately without overwatering?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce checking soil moisture before watering
decisionPoints.ifNo: Demonstrate proper water amounts using measuring tools

closing.activity: Care commitment ceremony - students promise to care for their plants daily

troubleshooting.then: Create visual reminder charts and partner buddy system

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning responsibility by helping care for plants at home or in the garden

lessons.title: Comment aider les animaux?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify ways to help animals by providing food, water, and safe spaces

opening.activity: Animal helping brainstorm - discussing ways students already help animals
opening.visualSupports: animal helping poster with safe and unsafe examples

main.activity: hands-on exploration creating bird feeders and discussing safe animal interactions
main.visualSupports: safe animal interaction chart, local wildlife identification cards

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand safety boundaries with wild animals?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore specific ways to help different types of animals
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on observing animals from distance and asking adults for help

closing.activity: Animal helper pledge - promising to help animals safely and kindly

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding why we don't touch wild animals
troubleshooting.then: Explain animals might be scared and prefer to be safe from humans

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how to safely help birds, pets, and other animals in their community

lessons.title: Notre jardin de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plant seeds and create a classroom garden to observe plant growth and practice care

opening.activity: Seed exploration - examining different seeds and predicting what will grow
opening.visualSupports: seed to plant growth chart, garden planning poster

main.activity: hands-on garden creation - planting seeds in individual containers and setting up class garden
main.visualSupports: planting step-by-step guide, garden layout diagram

decisionPoints.question: Are students planting at appropriate depths for their seed types?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them predict and record expected growth timeline
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use seed packet instructions to guide proper planting depth

closing.activity: Garden blessing ceremony - students share hopes for their plants' growth

troubleshooting.then: Use time-lapse videos or picture sequences showing seed germination

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning where food comes from and how gardens help provide for living things

lessons.title: Observer la croissance de nos plantes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will measure and record plant growth over time using simple tools and observations

opening.activity: Growth detective work - examining plants for signs of growth and change
opening.visualSupports: plant growth observation chart with measurement examples

main.activity: hands-on scientific measurement and recording of plant height, leaf count, and observations
main.visualSupports: measurement technique posters, growth tracking templates

decisionPoints.question: Can students accurately measure plant height using simple tools?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce comparing growth rates between different plants
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use non-standard units like paper clips or blocks for easier measurement

closing.activity: Growth celebration - sharing exciting observations and measurements with the class

troubleshooting.then: Partner students and use colorful measuring strips for easier reading

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how scientists track changes in living things over time

lessons.title: Les humains ont des besoins aussi
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify human needs (food, water, air, shelter) and compare them to plant and animal needs

opening.activity: Daily needs reflection - students share what they needed today to feel healthy and happy
opening.visualSupports: human needs poster matching plant and animal needs layout

main.activity: hands-on comparison activity creating three-way chart of plant, animal, and human needs
main.visualSupports: Venn diagram showing overlapping needs, needs comparison posters

decisionPoints.question: Do students recognize similarities between human and animal/plant needs?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore why all living things need similar basic requirements
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use concrete examples like everyone needing water to drink

closing.activity: Living things connection circle - students share one way they're similar to plants or animals

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: making connections between different living things
troubleshooting.then: Use physical actions - everyone breathing, drinking, eating motions

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding why families provide food, water, homes, and fresh air for health

lessons.title: Créer un habitat pour les petites créatures
lessons.oneGoal: Students will design and create a simple habitat that provides what small creatures need to survive

opening.activity: Habitat exploration - examining pictures of animal homes and discussing what makes them suitable
opening.visualSupports: habitat examples poster showing different animal homes

main.activity: hands-on habitat construction for beneficial insects or small creatures using natural materials
main.visualSupports: habitat building guide, creature care instruction cards

decisionPoints.question: Are students including all necessary habitat elements (food, water, shelter, air)?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Challenge them to explain why each element helps the creature survive
decisionPoints.ifNo: Guide them through creature needs checklist before building

closing.activity: Habitat showcase - students present their habitat and explain design choices

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding what makes a good habitat
troubleshooting.then: Compare to their own bedroom - what makes it comfortable and safe

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how gardens, parks, and natural areas provide what animals need

lessons.title: Nos plantes après plusieurs semaines
lessons.oneGoal: Students will evaluate their plant care success and identify what helped or hindered plant growth

opening.activity: Plant health assessment - students examine their plants for signs of health or problems
opening.visualSupports: healthy vs unhealthy plant comparison chart

main.activity: hands-on evaluation comparing plant growth results and analyzing care effectiveness
main.visualSupports: plant care success indicators chart, troubleshooting guide poster

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify specific factors that affected their plant's health?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them create recommendations for future plant care
decisionPoints.ifNo: Guide them through systematic comparison of care practices

closing.activity: Plant care wisdom sharing - students offer advice based on their experiences

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: connecting care actions to plant outcomes
troubleshooting.then: Use visual timeline showing care activities and plant changes over time

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning from gardening experiences and understanding what makes plants thrive

lessons.title: Célébrer les êtres vivants
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a class presentation showing what they learned about caring for living things

opening.activity: Learning celebration preparation - students review their growth and discoveries about living things
opening.visualSupports: unit learning journey timeline poster

main.activity: hands-on presentation creation showcasing plant care success and living thing knowledge
main.visualSupports: presentation organization template, showcase example displays

decisionPoints.question: Are students able to articulate what they learned about caring for living things?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them include specific examples and evidence of their learning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide sentence starters and visual cues to support sharing

closing.activity: Learning celebration - students share their favorite discovery about living things

troubleshooting.then: Use picture sequences and provide presentation structure templates

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing knowledge about caring for living things with family and community

lessons.title: Les saisons et les besoins des vivants
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore how the needs of living things change with different seasons

opening.activity: Seasonal observation walk - noticing how plants and animals adapt to current season
opening.visualSupports: seasonal changes poster showing plant and animal adaptations

main.activity: hands-on exploration of seasonal adaptations through pictures, stories, and comparisons
main.visualSupports: four seasons chart with living thing changes, adaptation example displays

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand that needs change but basic requirements stay the same?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore specific seasonal adaptations like thick fur or leaf changes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on how living things still need food, water, shelter in all seasons

closing.activity: Seasonal needs discussion - sharing observations about how living things change with seasons

troubleshooting.then: Connect to their own clothing changes and activities in different seasons

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding why gardens change seasonally and animals behave differently in winter

lessons.title: Protéger les habitats
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify ways humans can protect natural habitats that living things need

opening.activity: Habitat protection discussion - exploring how humans can help or hurt natural spaces
opening.visualSupports: helpful vs harmful human actions poster

main.activity: hands-on exploration creating action plans for protecting local habitats and living things
main.visualSupports: habitat protection action chart, local conservation examples display

decisionPoints.question: Can students connect simple actions to habitat protection?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Help them plan specific actions they can take in their community
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on basic concepts like not littering and being gentle with nature

closing.activity: Habitat protector pledge - students commit to specific actions to help living things

troubleshooting.then: Use concrete examples like picking up trash helps keep water clean for animals

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how families can help protect parks, forests, and natural areas

lessons.title: Les êtres vivants qui nous aident
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore how different living things help humans and other living things survive

opening.activity: Helper living things brainstorm - discussing plants and animals that help humans daily
opening.visualSupports: living things helpers poster with examples and benefits

main.activity: hands-on exploration of interdependence through matching games and relationship mapping
main.visualSupports: interdependence web display, helper relationships chart

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand that living things help each other, not just humans?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore complex relationships like bees helping flowers while getting food
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on obvious examples like pets helping families feel happy

closing.activity: Gratitude circle - students thank different living things for their help

troubleshooting.then: Use friendship examples - how friends help each other in different ways

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how bees help flowers, trees help clean air, and pets help families

lessons.title: Devenir des experts en soins
lessons.oneGoal: Students will teach younger students or family members about caring for living things

opening.activity: Expert preparation - students review their knowledge and practice explaining plant and animal care
opening.visualSupports: teaching tips poster, expert knowledge checklist

main.activity: hands-on teaching practice through peer instruction and demonstration of care techniques
main.visualSupports: teaching sequence cards, student expert badges

decisionPoints.question: Are students confident in explaining living thing needs clearly?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have them create their own teaching materials and demonstrations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide structured teaching scripts and visual aids for support

closing.activity: Expert certification ceremony - celebrating students as living things care experts

troubleshooting.then: Partner students and provide specific phrases they can use when teaching

lessons.realWorldConnection: Building confidence by teaching family members about plant and animal care

main.activity: hands-on celebration with family presentations, plant displays, and demonstration of care skills
main.visualSupports: celebration program, student achievement certificates

decisionPoints.question: Are students proudly demonstrating their plant care skills and knowledge?

closing.activity: Guardian commitment renewal - students pledge to continue caring for living things beyond the classroom

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en sciences
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Les êtres vivants autour de nous, De quoi ont besoin les plantes pour vivre?, Expérience: les plantes et l'eau, Les plantes ont besoin de lumière, De quoi ont besoin les animaux pour vivre?

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Encouragez les questions 'pourquoi' et explorez ensemble les réponses.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

La curiosité scientifique commence à la maison!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
